articles.headline: Poole and Smith Approach Contract Decisions as Season Closes
articles.dek: Alpha Prime Racing evaluates its driver roster with Brennan Poole reaching the end of his current agreement.
articles.body:
The conclusion of the thirty-three race schedule brings contract statuses into focus across the garage. Poole finished the season sixty-third in overall performance metrics while maintaining a happy status regarding his current contract expiration.

Teammate Lavar Scott remains signed through 2028. Sources indicate frustration within the camp regarding overall performance output this year. Team management faces decisions on how to restructure technical alliances before January testing.

Elsewhere, part-time competitor Garrett Smithley finishes his stint at SS-Green Light Racing. His agreement concludes at the end of 2027. paddock observers note that full-time opportunities in lower series or part-time entries remain open for discussion as the winter break begins.

articles.headline: Reviewing the 2027 Season Through Final Points and Win Totals
articles.dek: A statistical look back at thirty-three races reveals how Carson Kvapil and Brent Crews separated themselves from the field.
articles.body:
The thirty-three race schedule is complete. Carson Kvapil stands atop the final standings with 1305 points and eleven victories. That total defines the year. No other driver reached double-digit wins.

Brent Crews finished second in the standings with 1120 points and six wins. Consistency matched raw speed for the runner-up. Crews completed the campaign by winning the Homestead-Miami finale, leading 71 laps in the process.

Further down the order, Sheldon Creed secured third with 1063 points and three wins. Taylor Gray took fourth with 1031 points and three wins, highlighted by a drive from twenty-fourth to sixth in the final event. Corey Day rounded out the top five with 993 points and one win.

The battle around the cutoff line defined the middle tier. Rajah Caruth claimed twelfth in points with 784, edging Jeb Burton by twelve markers. Burton missed the top twelve despite a strong runner-up finish at Homestead where he led 36 laps.

Equipment attrition shaped the final afternoon. William Sawalich exited with a transmission failure, while Sheldon Creed retired due to suspension damage. Chandler Smith fell out following an accident.
articles.author: Wes Ostrander

articles.headline: Crews Wins Homestead Finale As Season Closes
articles.dek: Brent Crews captured the victory in the Hard Rock Bet 300 at Homestead-Miami Speedway as the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series concluded its thirty-third round.
articles.body:
Brent Crews drove his number 19 machine to victory lane in the season-ending Hard Rock Bet 300 at Homestead-Miami Speedway, securing his sixth win of the year. Crews led 71 laps over the course of the 200-lap event, holding off a charging Jeb Burton at the finish line to win by a margin of 1.215 seconds.

Jeb Burton finished second after starting nineteenth and leading 36 laps, while Carson Kvapil rounded out the podium in third place after leading 25 laps and locking down the championship title. Sammy Smith finished fourth and Brandon Jones completed the top five. Taylor Gray earned hard charger honors by climbing from his twenty-fourth starting position up to sixth at the checkered flag.

The race saw ten caution periods slow the pace, collecting several notable contenders along the way. Attrition played a major role in the closing stages as Sheldon Creed dropped out due to suspension failure, Chandler Smith exited following an accident, and William Sawalich parked his car early with transmission issues.

Carson Kvapil officially closed out the championship campaign with 1305 points and eleven victories. Brent Crews finished second in the final standings with 1120 points, followed by Sheldon Creed with 1063 points and Taylor Gray with 1031 points.

The O'Reilly Auto Parts Series now enters the offseason, with teams and drivers preparing for the next year of sim racing competition.
articles.author: Jamie Kowalski

articles.headline: Chandler Smith Jumps to Sam Hunt Racing for 2027 O'Reilly Auto Parts Series Campaign
articles.dek: The silly season landscape shifts as Chandler Smith secures a move to the Sam Hunt Racing stable for the upcoming season.
articles.body:
The 2027 NASCAR O'Reilly Auto Parts Series preseason is officially underway, and the garage is already reacting to major changes. Silly season has delivered its first significant blow with the confirmation that Chandler Smith is changing teams. Per a team source, Smith is moving up to the O'Reilly Auto Parts Series and will pilot the number 26 machine for Sam Hunt Racing.

This move marks a fresh chapter for Smith, who previously competed with Front Row Motorsports. Shifting over to Sam Hunt Racing means adapting to a new shop, a new crew, and the unique challenges of building chemistry before the season opener. For a team like Sam Hunt Racing, landing a driver of Smith's caliber signals clear intent to elevate their weekly competitiveness as the new year looms.

Looking ahead to the upcoming 33-race calendar, this pairing will be under immediate scrutiny. The equipment change shifts expectations immediately, and the garage will be watching closely to see how quickly Smith can adapt to his new surroundings. With the season set to begin, all eyes turn to the track to see if this offseason gamble pays off right out of the gate.
articles.author: Marcy Teague

chase.headline: Looking Ahead to the Next Campaign
chase.summary: With thirty-three events in the books, Carson Kvapil wraps up the top spot with 1305 points. Brent Crews secures the second position at 1120 points, holding strong as the championship dust settles.

notes.carson kvapil: Finished the year on top with 1305 points and locked down the number one ranking.
notes.brent crews: Claimed 1120 points to secure second in the final standings.
notes.sheldon creed: Rounded out the top three with 1063 points after a solid overall run.

race.headline: Season Finale in the Books
race.summary: Brent Crews closed out the year by taking the checkered flag at Homestead. Taylor Gray also made noise by charging up eighteen spots to take sixth.

notes.brent crews: Drove to victory lane to cap off the final race of the season in style.
notes.taylor gray: Punched his way forward by eighteen positions from twenty-fourth to finish sixth.
notes.carson kvapil: Collected a third-place run and paced the field for 25 circuits.

season.headline: Reflecting on Thirty-Three Rounds
season.summary: Carson Kvapil proved untouchable over the full schedule, claiming the crown by a wide margin. The rest of the field simply had to race for position behind him.

notes.carson kvapil: Dominant all year long, finishing with a massive 1305 points.
notes.brent crews: Put together a great runner-up campaign with 1120 points.
notes.rajah caruth: Worked hard all season to land inside the top twelve with 784 points.
